editionLabel: Mindclash English Essential Edition rules, copyright 2021
location: Cover; player setup step 16; Action Rounds; Next Era; Starting Asset Draft; credits and edition scope
firstPlayerRule: With standard setup, whoever most recently experienced déjà vu goes first.
officialTieBreak: The standard déjà vu criterion has no stated tie-break. In the Starting Asset Draft variant only, a tied total is broken in favor of the player holding the lowest-numbered card.
clarifications: Place that player’s banner beside the World Council spaces. Action turns proceed clockwise.
The optional Starting Asset Draft replaces this criterion: add the numbers on your four selected cards, and the lowest total starts the first Era.
The same player starts the next Era unless somebody has taken the relevant World Council action.
This entry covers the multiplayer Essential Edition. Its separate solo and expansion rules are outside this answer.
evidenceNotes: All seven listed pages were visually inspected. The publisher identifies Essential Edition as the core 2–4-player base game in its product-structure article at https://mindclashgames.com/news/the-new-product-line-up/, which was read on 2026-09-23. The optional card-draft criterion and its tie-break are explicitly separated from standard setup. The base personal-history criterion is portable; the variant is not used by the generic mix.

location: Cover; player setup step 4; gameplay; two-player rules; credits
firstPlayerRule: Whoever most recently saw a shooting star goes first.
clarifications: Give that player the First Player token; they retain it throughout the game.
Turns proceed clockwise.
The additional two-player Dream phase does not change this starting criterion. This answer covers the multiplayer rulebook.
evidenceNotes: The publisher’s game page directly links this websafe rulebook. It is not the earlier preview PDF or the separate Myths of the Night Sky storybook. All five listed PDF pages were visually inspected; spread numbering differs from printed numbering.

location: Cover; player setup; Starting Fame Points and Initiative Order; Set Initiative Order; Place Characters; credits
firstPlayerRule: Randomize the players’ markers on the Initiative Order track. The player in its first position acts first.
clarifications: The person who last wore a top hat chooses a Magician first during setup, with that choice proceeding clockwise. This does not determine the opening Initiative Order.
With two players, use the first and third Initiative Order spaces.
Character placement follows Initiative Order after simultaneous assignment planning.
In later turns, lower Fame means earlier initiative. Players tied on Fame reverse their relative order. Skip this reordering in the first turn.
houseFallback: If your group wants a different setup method, agree on one before play. That would be a house rule; the cited opening Initiative Order is already random.
evidenceNotes: All six cited pages were visually inspected. The top-hat sentence selects initial Magician-choice order only. Page 10 separately randomizes opening Initiative Order, and pages 11–12 confirm the first-turn exception and action sequence. Later Fame ties and the game-winning tie-break must not be presented as opening selection rules. The separate solo expansion manual is outside this entry. Directory only: actual opening order is random.

location: Cover; player setup steps 10–14; Select Action and Resolve Action; End of Season; solo player setup; credits
firstPlayerRule: In multiplayer, whoever most recently made a mixed drink is the starting player.
clarifications: Give that player the Starting Player token. Players choose and reveal Action cards simultaneously, then resolve their actions in clockwise turn order.
Initial Leader placement proceeds counterclockwise from the last player. In the Full Game, the starting Spell choices and Ritual-marker placement use that same reverse order.
At the end of Autumn, Winter and Spring, pass the Starting Player token clockwise.
In solo play, you take the Starting Player token at setup.
evidenceNotes: The publisher directly links the public Dropbox manual. The first bounded download exceeded 70 MB and was not used. A complete 113,488,684-byte retrieval succeeded under a 120 MB limit; its hash was recorded. All six listed pages were visually inspected. The mixed-drink instruction is part of both Basic and Full setup, outside the Full Game-only box. No alcoholic-content condition or definition of mixed drink was invented. Ordered action resolution distinguishes this from an entirely simultaneous game.

location: Cover and two-episode scope; Before Starting Play; credits
firstPlayerRule: For a standalone multiplayer game of Episode 1, whoever was most recently on a boat goes first.
clarifications: Regular turns proceed clockwise.
Preliminary Settlement and Influence placement runs in reverse: start with the last player and proceed counterclockwise.
Episode 2 has a different criterion. This entry does not cover the separate Chronicle campaign or solo mode.
evidenceNotes: All three listed pages were visually inspected. The cover explicitly identifies two standalone episodes in the Episodes 1 & 2 box, so this and Episode 2 map to one inventory identity rather than two completed games. The reverse preliminary placement does not change the stated clockwise regular-turn order. No newer second-edition claim is inferred from the current product page.

location: Cover and episode scope; Before Starting Play and Turn Structure; credits
firstPlayerRule: For a standalone multiplayer game of Episode 2, whoever most recently went on a nature adventure goes first.
clarifications: Regular turns proceed clockwise.
Preliminary Settlement or Camp placement and its associated benefits run counterclockwise, beginning with the last player.
Episode 1 uses a different criterion. This entry does not cover the separate Chronicle campaign or solo mode.
evidenceNotes: All three listed pages were visually inspected. The title, cover and credits distinguish Episode 2; Episode 1’s inspected cover identifies both as standalone games in the same Episodes 1 & 2 box. Nature adventure is not given a narrower invented definition. The current product page’s second-edition wording was not substituted for the copyright-2021 source identity.
